feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
BIP118 introduces a proposal where the commitment to transaction inputs is handled in a specific manner. The approach involves blanking certain fields, but it notably retains the value of the input being spent. This design decision ensures that while selected aspects of the input may not be committed, the actual input value remains an explicit part of the transaction structure.
Blanking the hashSequence field is highlighted as a necessary component for most practical use-cases involving NOINPUT, suggesting that omitting this step could undermine the intended functionality. By maintaining a commitment to the value and outputs, the protocol avoids scenarios where unexpected transaction fees arise, thereby preserving the integrity and predictability of transaction costs. This careful balance between flexibility and security underpins the rationale behind the current formulation of BIP118.
